images.title: Hubble radius — original Hubble-law explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG diagram from cited scientific facts; rasterized to 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 px-wide thumbnail. Derives R = c/H₀ algebraically from v = H₀d. Dimensionless axes. The circle denotes a distance marker, not an opaque shell or visibility boundary.

images.title: One-nanometer transistor gate — original device cross-section schematic
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG diagram from cited scientific facts; rasterized to 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 px-wide thumbnail. Original geometric schematic of the reported 2016 MoS₂ channel, carbon-nanotube gate, ZrO₂ insulator and SiO₂ support. Only 1 nm nanotube diameter is dimensioned. No source artwork or microscopy pixels copied.

images.title: Boötes Void — original conceptual underdensity illustration
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG diagram from cited scientific facts; rasterized to 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 px-wide thumbnail. Source caption describes an underdense region and foreground galaxies. The source map itself is BY-SA and was NOT copied. This is an original explanatory sketch with explicitly illustrative dots; no measured density field, member catalog, size or boundary is implied.

images.title: One light-year — original explanatory distance diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG diagram from cited scientific facts; rasterized to 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 px-wide thumbnail. NASA Space Place defines one light-year as the distance light travels in one Earth year. The wave is symbolic; no physical wavelength, cosmic expansion model or numerical conversion is claimed.

images.title: Helium-4 nucleus — original rms charge-diameter diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG; rendered to 1200 × 800 JPEG and a 300 × 200 thumbnail. NIST lists an alpha-particle rms charge radius of 1.6785(21) fm. The displayed diameter is twice this radius, rounded to 3.36 fm. The soft cloud is illustrative and the dashed circle marks an rms radius, not a nuclear surface or an enclosed-charge fraction.

images.title: PSR J0437-4715 — original NICER equatorial-diameter diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG; rendered to 1200 × 800 JPEG and a 300 × 200 thumbnail. NASA's 22 August 2024 NICER summary gives an inferred equatorial radius of 11.36 km with 5–8% uncertainties. The diameter is twice the reported central radius, 22.72 km, shown as approximately 22.7 km. This is explicitly the 2024 result used by the dataset, not a claim to be a new radius analysis. Sphere color and coordinate grid are illustrative; no hot-spot geometry is invented.

images.title: Milky Way central bar — original long-bar measurement schematic
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG; rendered to 1200 × 800 JPEG and a 300 × 200 thumbnail. Wegg, Gerhard and Portail (2015) infer a 5.0 ± 0.2 kpc half-length for their two-component bar and an angle of 28–33 degrees to the Sun–center line. The diagram uses an approximately 10 kpc full length and 30-degree orientation. Random star glyphs, the bar width and the Sun's radial placement are illustrative, explicitly not measured catalog positions. No spiral-arm geometry is asserted.

images.title: Baryon acoustic oscillation scale — original galaxy-pair separation diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original explanatory diagram)
images.changes: New original SVG; rendered to 1200 × 800 JPEG and a 300 × 200 thumbnail. DESI describes BAO as a slight excess of tracer pairs separated by about 150 Mpc, inherited from early-plasma sound waves. The diagram labels one present-day comoving pair separation, not a bubble diameter. The galaxy glyphs are illustrative, not a catalog or a measured pair. No numerical correlation-function data are invented or plotted.

images.title: String Length — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Conceptual open and closed strings, not a photograph, measured geometry, physical cord, or fixed universal string-length prediction. No numerical string/Planck equivalence is asserted.

images.title: Carbon Atom — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. 140 pm is twice the tabulated 70 pm empirical atomic radius. Cloud/lobes are qualitative, not an ab initio density, enclosed-probability contour or literal surface. Nucleus enlarged.

images.title: Hyperion — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Guinness reports Hyperion at 116.07 m in 2019, rounded here to approximately 116 m. Original generic coast-redwood silhouette, not a verified photograph or reconstruction of its crown. Does not corroborate the dataset’s unsourced 116.2 m / 2026 claim.

images.title: Spongy Surface (PIA17194)
images.author: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute
images.changes: NASA Photojournal JPEG retained at 1024 x 1024; generated 300 px-wide thumbnail. Processed Cassini narrow-angle image of Hyperion captured May 31, 2015, during the final close approach to this irregular moon; not a review composite.

images.title: Longest Lightning Flash — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. WMO reports 829 ± 8 km for the 22 October 2017 US megaflash, measured by maximum great-circle separation. Authored channels/clouds are conceptual, not satellite data or traced channel geometry.

images.title: Kuiper Belt — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. NASA places the main belt at approximately 30–50 AU, hence approximately 100 AU outer diameter. Original face-on annulus is a regional schematic, with no synthetic catalog points. Band edges are approximate and do not delimit all trans-Neptunian objects.

images.title: Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The paper reports 14 of 31 GRBs at 1.6 < z < 2.1 in roughly 1/8 of the sky and infers a 2000–3000 Mpc span. A simple count strip conveys those published counts, not measured angular positions, structure membership or a mapped boundary. The proposed wall is explicitly disputed; no galaxy-wall artwork is copied.

images.title: DVD Track Pitch — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. ECMA-267 specifies a 0.74 µm nominal track pitch (±0.03 µm). Parallel strips are a locally straightened view of adjacent spiral turns; drawn mark widths, lengths and sequence are illustrative, not a micrograph or encoded data.

images.title: Prelude FLNG — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Shell states 488 m length and 74 m width. The bounding hull proportions follow those dimensions; hull contours and generic equipment symbols are original illustrative design, not a traced Shell rendering, photograph or as-built deck layout. No qualifying facility photo was established in the prior images3 search.

images.title: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The opened Guinness record page gives the bridge length rounded to 164 km; this image uses that coarse figure rather than claiming the page states 164.8 km. The ruler represents total length, while the generic viaduct segment and train are illustrative, not a route map, engineering elevation or claim that the pictured segment spans 164 km. Prior images3 photo candidates were BY-SA or all rights reserved.

images.title: Credit Card — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. ID-1 length 85.60 mm and width 53.98 mm. Original unbranded card with generic chip motif; no actual account, personal data, company logo or copied card design. Corner shape and chip geometry are illustrative.

images.title: Weak Force Range — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Using PDG 2024 W mass 80.3692 GeV/c² and NIST ℏc = 197.3269804 MeV fm gives ℏ/(mW c) ≈ 2.45526e-18 m. Curve is exp(-r/range), the exponential factor only, not the full Yukawa potential or a force measurement.

images.title: Muonic Hydrogen Atom — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The FAMU paper states a ground-state muonic Bohr radius of about 285 fm, including proton–muon reduced mass. Twice this radius is approximately 570 fm = 0.57 pm. Cloud is schematic, not bounded at aμ, and the proton dot is enlarged. This diameter is a convention, not the full wavefunction extent.

images.title: Tau Compton Wavelength — original explanatory diagram
images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
images.changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Ordinary (not reduced) Compton wavelength h/(mc), displayed as 0.698 fm, rounded from CODATA 2022. A single sine-wave glyph explains a length, with arbitrary amplitude; it is not a particle boundary, observed field oscillation, de Broglie wavelength or emitted-photon measurement.

images.author: Universe Scales (original artwork)

images.title: Lolong skeleton at the National Museum of Natural History, Manila
images.author: Judgefloro
images.changes: Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Creator’s source page identifies the Lolong museum exhibit, including replica and skeleton, and explicitly dedicates the photograph under CC0. The selected frame visibly shows the suspended crocodile skeleton; the caption explicitly identifies a skeleton display rather than the living animal. No claim that photographic perspective measures his full 6.17 m body length.

images.title: AMNH titanosaur skeletal cast
images.author: D. Benjamin Miller
images.changes: Cropped downloaded source to [0, 0, 3000, 836]; Lifted shadows using gamma 0.78; Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons identifies this as the titanosaur skeleton cast at AMNH, photographed 18 January 2016, and the creator dedicates it under CC0. Used the original creator’s image, not the BY-SA derivative AMNHTitanosaur-03.jpg. Crop retains the visible head-to-tail cast and removes the separate fossil display on the right.

images.title: Individual sand grains through a microscope
images.author: Thelasthedgehog
images.changes: Cropped downloaded source to [130, 430, 830, 1230]; Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Source identifies microscopic observation of smooth sand and licenses the photograph CC BY 4.0. Crop isolates the resolved grains and excludes the dark eyepiece surroundings. No scale bar is invented; the pictured grains are not claimed to be exactly the representative 1 mm catalog size.

images.title: El Reno tornado in its multiple-vortex stage, 31 May 2013
images.author: Richard Thompson / NOAA Storm Prediction Center
images.changes: Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons describes the El Reno 31 May 2013 tornado in its multiple-vortex stage, credits Richard Thompson at SPC, and marks it PD-USGov. The image itself carries the event/date/SPC attribution. It shows the tornado, not the parent storm from orbit; visible funnels are not asserted to outline the maximum damage width.

images.title: Chloroplast cutaway illustration
images.author: DataBase Center for Life Science (DBCLS)
images.changes: Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons identifies an isolated chloroplast illustration by DBCLS, originally doi:10.7875/togopic.2017.50, under CC BY 4.0 with a completed license review. This is a teaching cutaway showing thylakoid stacks, not a micrograph or measured architecture.

images.title: Hunga Tonga eruption plume, Himawari-8, 15 January 2022 05:20 UTC
images.author: Japan Meteorological Agency (Himawari-8); Digital Typhoon / NII
images.changes: Selected animation frame 80 (zero-based); Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Source is the JMA / Digital Typhoon animation with explicit CC BY 4.0 terms, also linked to the compatible Japanese government data terms. Zero-based frame 80 visibly reads 2022-01-15 05:20:00 UTC and shows a large textured umbrella plume. Frame was fully decoded/composited by Pillow before export. Top-down view does not directly measure the plume’s height.

images.title: TRAPPIST-1 system versus the Solar System — orbit comparison
images.author: NASA, ESA, CSA, Joseph Olmsted (STScI)
images.changes: Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. NASA’s asset caption explicitly identifies all seven planet orbits b–h and compares their compact orbital span with the inner Solar System. This is the 2026 orbital comparison diagram, not a travel poster or a literal photograph of exoplanets. NASA image-use guidance applies (the Hubble/Webb copyright pages redirect there); the asset has no third-party copyright notice.

images.title: Andromeda gaseous halo and 43 background-quasar sightlines — illustration
images.author: NASA, ESA, and E. Wheatley (STScI)
images.changes: Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. NASA identifies this as a gas-halo illustration with the 43 background quasars used to probe absorption, not an optical image of visible halo gas. The source title says Illustration; the new caption preserves that distinction. NASA image-use guidance applies (Hubble copyright page redirects there); no third-party copyright notice appears on the asset.

images.title: Complete yeast 80S ribosome — original coordinate-based illustration
images.author: Universe Scales (rendering); Ben-Shem et al. (2011), PDB 4V88 (structural data)
images.changes: New CPU rendering of biological assembly 1 of PDB 4V88 using the existing authored GLB; includes the complete deposited yeast 80S particle and Stm1. RNA gold; protein chain colors illustrative. Smooth surface is a display envelope around atomic sites, not experimental electron density. Unresolved residues, waters and ions omitted. JPEG 1200 × 800; matching 300 × 200 thumbnail.
